meta_description: Qubit is a cooperative quantum deduction game for 3–6 players. Decode the hidden Quantum Code using partial wavelength clues before your quantum state decoheres.
og_title: Qubit — Cooperative Quantum Deduction | Tech CoLab
og_description: Work as a team to identify an 8-qubit quantum code from partial clues. Avoid decoherence. One measurement — make it count.
hero_sub: A cooperative deduction game where each teammate holds a different wavelength clue. Combine partial information to locate the hidden qubit state — before environmental noise collapses everything.

features.title: 16×16 Quantum Matrix
features.body: 256 cells. Each represents an 8-qubit state. Row nibble × 16 + column nibble = decimal. Navigate the lattice with region boundaries, dark/light shading, and digit-sum constraints.

features.title: Partial Information Deduction
features.body: Each player holds a private wavelength clue from one of 6 color-coded sheets. No player can solve it alone — only by combining perspectives can the team narrow to one cell.

features.title: Environment Deck Pressure
features.body: Every proposed cell draws an environment card. CASCADE forces all players to verify. NOISE advances decoherence. Three noise events = mission failure.

features.title: Cooperative Teamwork
features.body: Unlike competitive games, everyone wins or loses together. There is no traitor — only the quantum system working against you.

how_it_works.label: Receive Your Clue
how_it_works.body: Each player privately sees clues from one wavelength color. You know which cells match your clue — but not your teammates'.

how_it_works.label: Propose & Token
how_it_works.body: The active player proposes a cell. They place a circle token if it matches their clue, or a square if it doesn't. Then an environment card is drawn.

how_it_works.label: Cascade or Pass
how_it_works.body: A CASCADE card means all other players also verify the cell against their clue, leaving their own tokens. Together the board fills with evidence.

how_it_works.label: Call Measurement
how_it_works.body: When the team is confident, the active player calls Measurement. Correct = mission accomplished. Wrong = immediate failure.

faq.a: 3 to 6 players. Each player count uses a different setup card with different clue assignments.

faq.q: How long does a game take?
faq.a: About 20–30 minutes once players understand the clue types.
Yes — each player's wavelength clue is private. You can discuss which cells match your clue but not the clue text itself.
In quantum computing, decoherence is when a qubit loses its quantum state due to environmental interference. In the game, three NOISE cards mean your quantum state has collapsed — mission failure.
